description: Prints the queued notifications once and empties the queue, or holds until one arrives within a time limit, then prints it. Refuses to start unless one of those two modes is chosen, and reports when an interrupt arrives during the hold.

Health check that tells whether the JavaScript runtime is new enough, whether the target folder accepts writes, what the previous execution left behind, and whether the install entry is present. It prints known caveats and succeeds only when the runtime, the folder and the entry all pass.
Turns an outcome into a category label: a success is classified by its state, and a failure is classified by its error label.

Test that starts the server in a temporary folder with the built-in server definitions turned off, sends it the session message in full, and checks that the whole message comes back as one recorded entry. It returns a pass with the number of space-separated parts, or a failure showing what the entry became, then deletes the temporary folder.

Builds a set of version control helpers for the project folder: runs its commands with a time limit, checks that each given location stays inside the folder and is not the whole folder, repeats network operations when a transient problem hits them, reads the checked-out line of history, and turns the upstream address into its provider label and owner/project pair. It also checks the continuous integration outcome for a commit, after validating the commit hash and project pattern.

Runs the loop for one session: each turn it assembles instructions from the stored guidance and latest history, asks the AI for its next moves, and records the answer. Moves run in sequence or can run alongside the next request, and the loop ends when a closing move arrives, the request fails, or the turn cap is hit, returning a final label and the supporting evidence.

Loads one named guide from the packaged guides folder: it gathers every member under that guide's folder with its address, a content fingerprint, how large it is and a text type, then requires the main markdown member and returns its parsed header, main text and member list. It throws when the main member is absent.

Starts the main serving loop for one agent session: it sets up the action handlers, replays stored evidence so repeated requests get the same answer, tracks requests still underway and the ones that were aborted, and sends a quiet notice after a fixed period with no requests. It also starts a watchdog that flags standing-requirement breaks, such as a request arriving before the first context load or a closing move with no evidence.

Builds three handlers for peer review: one assembles a bundle from a specification and a list of references, one records a signer's ruling on a bundle with optional remarks, and one joins every recorded entry into a serialized string cut down to one page. Each loads its review code only the first time it is called.

Opens the event journal for a session folder if one is already there, refreshing its standing requirements, or creates a new journal with them and the descriptive fields otherwise. It reports whether an existing journal was reused.

Creates the document-level action routines for a project folder: reading pages of a document by line numbers or by character positions, serving built-in guide addresses, writing whole documents, and editing by exact replacement of a span. Every location must stay within the folder, including when reached through links, and the set tracks detached work and the action requests still underway.

Writes a markdown reference of the browser-related actions: for each one it gives its summary and every input parameter with its value kind, whether it must be supplied, the allowed choices, and what it means. The heading notes that these are called as functions on a shared handle, and that the browser action takes plain text as its payload.

Chooses which parameter name a named action takes its free text in. It uses the default text name unless the action lists a separate summary parameter and does not list the default text name, in which case it uses the summary one.

Works out what a browser command needs: for the browser-events command it returns the working folder, the requested operation and the named browsing context, while for the browser and chrome commands it scans the text for screenshot locations and returns them with the working folder, or nothing when none are found. Any other command gives nothing back.

Brings the project folder and each nested repository that exists in step with its upstream, one at a time, and collects one outcome per folder, turning any unexpected failure into its own outcome. It appends the whole collection as one line to a history file, ignoring a write failure, adds a status note with the number of folders moved forward and the number passed over, and returns the collection.

Turns a line-range edit request into a full document write: it rejects locations that are absolute or climb out of the project folder, rejects a first or last number that is missing or falls outside the document, and requires new wording unless the range is being removed. It then joins the untouched rows around the new ones and returns the write request carrying the whole new document, or a rejection that changes nothing.

Lists the folders a request may touch: the base folder found for it, plus any folders its payload gives, each located relative to that base and kept once. It returns an empty list when no base folder can be found.

Adds a cut-off notice to a code search reply when it displays fewer hits than the full tally it reports: the notice gives how many were omitted and how to request all of them, naming the default cap when that caused the cut. Any other command, a reply with no hit list, or one with nothing omitted passes through unchanged.

Lists the workers holding a claim on a project folder: it scans the claim markers for that folder, removes any marker whose claim file is gone, and reports for each remaining worker its id, its process ID and whether that process is still running. It gives an empty list when the claim directory does not exist and nothing when it cannot be read.

Decides whether a reply is clean: it must be a plain object with no failure field set, including the record-keeping and monitoring ones, must not have hit its time limit, and must not be marked as not succeeded. If it carries a nested inner object, that object is checked the same way, and the answer is true only when every check passes.

Stops a closing request for a tracked work row when that row's record names no sources: in that case it returns a declined reply with a sequence number and the reason, otherwise it returns nothing so the closing request goes ahead.

Works out the address for the optional web transport: the connection point comes from a command switch, then an environment setting, then a built-in default, and it is accepted only when it is an integer of zero or more, with zero allowed only if someone set it deliberately. The machine address follows the same order and falls back to its own built-in default.
Builds a lookup table from each running process ID to its launch line, using a fresh snapshot of the system's process list gathered asynchronously.

Finds connection numbers where more than one guard process is running: for each such number it chooses which process to keep, lists the rest as extra copies, and returns the reports ordered by number. A number with a single guard process gives no report.

Adds a startup section to a text answer the first time a session asks for one in a project folder: it leaves alone answers that are not text, that have failed, that are bracketed lists, or that already received the section, and if adding it throws, it keeps the original text and notes the failure.

Clears a leftover install note from a folder: it reads the note, and when the note records a version that looks like a proper version number (after removing any leading byte-order mark), it deletes the note and adds a journal entry naming the note and that version. Anything else leaves the note in place.

Starts a background update check for two components: when it actually replaces one, it prints a line naming the old and new version and where the earlier copy was kept, and when it nudges the shared background process to reload it prints the process number. A failed check is noted in the journal and the installed copies stay as they are.
Returns the full location of the installed server package file inside the shared support folder.

Clears the saved records for one connection point: it checks three records, and for each one whose recorded process IDs are all dead it deletes that record. It returns true only when every record was deleted, and any record naming a still running process is kept and makes the result false.

Reads the current phase of a project folder: it asks for the phase and whether any queued rows remain, each within a time allowance, then returns the phase with a true or false flag for the queued rows. If the folder location is not absolute, or the phase does not come back in time, it returns a not-determined answer with the explanation.

Sets up the server program at startup: it keeps serving when an asynchronous failure happens, records how signals end the program, keeps the output channel free for protocol messages, survives the client disconnecting, exits when the parent goes away, and writes a startup journal entry with the build tag, launch arguments, folder and runtime release. It always returns true.
